text:
maria: alert: CPU and syscall rate up on host pool after rolling adaptive-batcher-v2 last night. tail on parse/token path during long streaming sessions.
raj: saw it too. error budget small bump, p95 CPU +18% on the ingest boxes.
owen: did we change kernel selector recently? iirc only batcher patched.
maria: correct, kernel selector untouched. batcher v2 tries to coalesce by 'logical chunks' instead of time windows -> more small-fragment aggregates.
jen: that could increase KV cache churn if fragment boundaries don't align with cached prefixes. more unique prefixes -> more parse work.
deploy-bot: Deployment 2026-04-12T03:12:07Z - adaptive-batcher-v2 -> canary-2/8 - SUCCESS
raj: pulled a flamegraph from a culprit host:

perf snippet:
parse_and_normalize     28.7%
kv_lookup               16.3%
tokenize                14.9%
http2_read              10.5%
syscall_readv           7.2%
others                  22.4%

maria: syscall_readv is weirdly high despite our writev coalesce change being on prod already. maybe opposite: many small reads rather than writes.
owen: can we repro locally? i made a small harness that mirrors chat streaming:
```
./stream-hammer --model=model-y --clients=12 --avg-msg=200 --chunk-lambda=0.2 --duration=3m
```
jen: repro shows similar flamegraph on my laptop VM when batcher toggled to logical-chunk mode. Also saw KV hit-rate drop: 97% -> 83% in stress window.
raj: hypothesis: logical-chunk coalescing delays emission until chunk assembly completes, but for streaming we break into lots of micro-chunks that invalidate cached prefix heuristics. batcher holds partial state and emits more variable-length fragments.
maria: suggestion: quick mitigations: 1) revert batcher-v2 on streaming tier 2) increase kvcache TTL/grace for prefix keys 3) enable an experimental "emit-fast-on-stream" flag that prefers smaller immediate emits for streaming sessions.
owen: i'm testing kvcache TTL + emit-fast-on-stream locally. early results: TTL +200ms gives +9% CPU drop and hit-rate back to ~93%.
jen: we should also add a tokenizer fast-path: if payload bytes are all single-byte ASCII and no control chars, skip utf8-normalize step. common in chat. cheap win.
raj: +1. i'll open PR for tokenizer-ascii-fastpath and add unit tests.
maria: longer term: kernel selector and batcher must be co-evaluated. the batcher change indirectly changed request shapes the selector sees which may alter chosen kernels (mini-batch sizes differ). add an experiment matrix before future rollouts.
owen: telemetry tasks: add histogram for logical-chunk sizes, prefix reuse ratio at kvcache keys, small-read syscall rate per host.
jen: also instrument a trace tag when batcher-v2 is active and when emit-fast-on-stream is used. makes slice comparisons easy.
maria: rollout plan: revert full batcher-v2 on streaming pool first; keep analyzer job to compare emit timings. rollback queued.
raj: created rollback PR: #4321 - revert adaptive-batcher-v2 for streaming-pool. will merge after smoke.
deploy-bot: Rollback PR #4321 merged by raj at 2026-04-12T04:10:21Z
maria: canary metrics after rollback: streaming pool p95 CPU down 12%, kvcache hit back to 95% on canary. Looks promising.
owen: followups: jen PR for ascii fastpath, raj PR for trace tag + batcher telemetry, maria to draft experiment matrix for selector+batcher combos.
jen: filing tokenizer PR now: tokenizer/fastpath-skip-normalize-if-ascii.
raj: i'll add a gating rule: any batcher or kernel picker change must run paired canary tests measuring kvcache hit ratio and syscall/readv patterns.
maria: thanks team. filing postmortem notes and schedule a short triage sync later today. :white_check_mark:
